body.translated_text: The extant portions of the text of <s>Āryadeva</s>'s [work]:

children.text: 1.21. śatruvat yānti te kālā niyamena kṣaṇādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 1.21. Those moments and other [units of time] pass by like enemies, in a fixed sequence;

children.text: sarvvathā tena te rāgaḥ śatrubhūteṣu teṣu mā // 21 //
children.translated_text: therefore, in every way, let there be no attachment toward them, who are [your] enemies. [Verse 21]
1.22. 'Out of fear of separation, I do not leave the house, [you] fool!'
Would any wise person do what should be done after deliberation, under compulsion? [Verse 22]

children.text: 2.7. śarīraṃ sucireṇāpi sukhasya svaṃ na jāyate /
children.translated_text: 2.7. Even after a long time, the body does not become its own [source] of pleasure;
the overpowering of one's own nature by another is simply not possible. [Verse 32]
2.8. For the foremost, suffering is mental; for the rest, it is bodily;
by this twofold suffering, the world is struck down day after day. [Verse 33]
2.9. Pleasure is subject to imagination, and from what is subject [to change] comes the imagination of suffering;
therefore there is nothing anywhere more powerful than suffering. [Verse 34]

children.text: 2.10. kālo yathā yathā yāti duḥkhavṛddhistatha tathā /
children.translated_text: 2.10. As time passes further and further, suffering increases correspondingly;
therefore, for this corpse [the body], pleasure appears as belonging to another. [Verse 35]
2.11. The causes of suffering that are seen — diseases and others — are as many [as they are];

children.text: tāvanto na tu dṛśyante narāṇāṃ sukhahetavaḥ // 36 //
children.translated_text: but the causes of pleasure for humans are not seen to be as many. [Verse 36]
2.12. Just as a reversal of increasing pleasure is observed,
there is no such reversal of increasing suffering. [Verse 37]
3.13. Someone with a missing nose might find satisfaction with a prosthetic nose;
similarly, attachment arises toward flowers and the like as a remedy for what is impure. [Verse 73]

children.text: 3.24. śuci nāma ca tadyuktaṃ vairāgyaṃ yatra jāyate /
children.translated_text: 3.24. That alone should be called 'pure' toward which dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) arises;

children.text: na ca so'sti kvacidbhāvo niyayād rāgakāraṇam // 74 //
children.translated_text: but there is no such entity that is by nature a cause of attachment. [Verse 74]
3.25. Impermanent (<s>anitya</s>), impure (<s>aśubha</s>), suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), and non-self (<s>anātman</s>) — these four
are all found together, in brief, in every single [thing]. [Verse 75]

children.text: 4.1. ahaṃ mameti vā darpaḥ sataḥ kasya bhaved bhave /
children.translated_text: 4.1. Who in this world could have pride thinking 'I' or 'mine,'

children.text: yasmāt sarvve'pi sāmānyā viṣayāḥ sarvva dehinām // 76 //
children.translated_text: since all objects are common to all embodied beings? [Verse 76]

children.text: 4.2. gaṇadāsasya te darpaḥ ṣaḍbhāgena bhṛtasya kaḥ /
children.translated_text: 4.2. What pride can you have, a servant of the masses, maintained by a sixth share [of the produce]?
The task to be done, wherever it may be, depends on the one appointed [to do it]. [Verse 77]

children.text: 4.14. ṛṣīṇāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ sarvva kurvīta na vicakṣaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: 4.14. A discerning person should not imitate all the deeds of the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages),
for among them too there exist inferior, middling, and superior [grades]. [Verse 89]

children.text: 4.15. putravat pālito lokaḥ purataḥ pārthivaiḥ śubhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 4.15. In former times, the world was protected like a son by virtuous kings;
today it has been made a hunting ground [for beasts] by those who follow the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Kali</s> [age]. [Verse 90]

children.text: 4.16. chidraprahāriṇaḥ pāpaṃ yadi rājño na vidyate /
children.translated_text: 4.16. If there is no sin for a king who strikes at [others'] vulnerabilities,

children.text: anyeṣāmapi caurāṇāṃ tat prāgeva na vidyate // 91 //
children.translated_text: then all the more so is there no sin for other thieves. [Verse 91]
4.17. The renunciation of all one's possessions is not honored in the case of liquor and the like;

children.text: ātmano'pi parityāgaḥ kiṃ manye pūjito raṇe // 92 //
children.translated_text: I wonder, then — is the renunciation of one's very self honored in battle? [Verse 92]

body.text: 4.23. vipro'pi karmmanā śūdraḥ kena manye na jāyate // 98 //
body.translated_text: 4.23. Even a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, I think, becomes a <s>śūdra</s> by [his] actions — by whom is [he] not [so] born? [Verse 98]

children.translated_text: 4.24. O king, there is no sharing of sovereignty as there is of sin;
what wise person would commit murder for the sake of another in the long run? [Verse 99]
4.25. Having seen others who are equal, superior, and powerful,

children.text: aiśvāryajanito mānaḥ satāṃ hṛdi na tiṣṭhati // 100 //
children.translated_text: pride born of sovereignty does not remain in the hearts of the good. [Verse 100]
5.1. There is no action whatsoever of the <s>Buddhas</s> that is without a cause;
even their breathing operates solely for the benefit of living beings. [Verse 101]
